title: FuzzyDate
description: A dateable point or span with explicit precision, used by events and relation time-bounds.

display.description: Human-readable form to render, e.g. '1963', 'August–September 1974', 'c. 1958', 'early 1970s'. Required on events; optional on relation time-bounds.

precision.description: . "century" is for pre-modern subjects, where the source itself can place a life or event no more closely than that -- an 8th-century alchemist's patronage, say. Widening sort_start/sort_end to the century's bounds keeps ordering honest instead of inventing a year nobody claimed "season" is for a source that dates something to a season rather than a month -- "summer 1964", "the following winter" -- which is common in recollection and correspondence. Widening sort_start/sort_end to the season's bounds keeps ordering honest; "month" would invent a precision the source never gave, and "range" loses that it was a named season.

sort_start.description: Earliest plausible ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Sort key only — not an assertion of exactness. Use day/month = 01 to represent an unknown day/month within the earliest bound.

sort_end.description: Latest plausible ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Equal to sort_start for a single fuzzy point.
